cues.text: Joining the boys
Homare Sawa was born in 1978 in Fuchū, a city in Tokyo, Japan.
When she was six, she went to watch her older brother train.
His coach saw her and invited her to join the boys’ team.
Kick the ball.
Homare said yes.
Playing with the boys, she learned to be quick, brave and clever with the ball.
She kept playing football with boys and with older players as she grew up, and it made her a tough and clever player.
Playing with people bigger than you can make you braver and smarter.
Young and ready
When Homare was only twelve, she played her first match in Japan’s top women’s league, for a club called Yomiuri Beleza.
In December 1993, at fifteen, she played for Japan for the first time, and she scored four goals against the Philippines.
She was much younger than most of the players around her.
Climb the steps.
Homare kept learning from older players, one step at a time.
She listened, watched and practised, and she became a key player for her club and her country.
Being young is not a reason to wait. Learn from the people around you.
Starting again far away
In 1999, her club in Japan ended her contract.
Homare decided to go and play in the United States, a long way from home, where people spoke a different language.
Open the suitcase.
From 2001 to 2003, she played for the Atlanta Beat in a new professional league in America.
Starting again in a new country is not easy, but she kept improving.
She had new teammates and a new way of playing to get used to, and she became an even better player.
When a door closes, you can be brave and try somewhere new.
A country in sadness
In March 2011, a huge earthquake and tsunami hit Japan.
Many people lost their homes, and many families were very sad.
A few months later, the World Cup began in Germany, and Homare was Japan’s captain.
Raise the banner.
The team dedicated the tournament to the people hit by the disaster.
Homare hoped that, if they never gave up on the pitch, the team could give people at home some courage.
In hard times, doing your best can lift other people too.
Never giving up
In the final, Japan played the United States.
In extra time, the United States scored to lead 2–1.
Then, in the 117th minute, with only a few minutes left, Homare scored.
It was 2–2!
Take the next penalty.
Japan won the penalty shootout 3–1.
They were the first Asian team ever to win the Women’s World Cup, and back at home, their win brought joy to a sad country.
Keep going until the very end. The game is not over until it is over.
Six World Cups
Homare won the Golden Ball for the best player of the 2011 World Cup, and the Golden Boot for the most goals: five.
Then FIFA named her the Women’s World Player of the Year.
She was the first Asian player, man or woman, to win such a big award.
Lift the photo frame.
Homare played in six World Cups, from 1995 to 2015, and she stopped playing at the end of 2015.
In her very last tournament, she won one more cup with her club.
She had played for Japan for twenty-two years.
Keep going for a long time, and you can do things nobody has done before.
